review_notes: I read the whole file and the related Mathlib GradedRingHom simp lemmas. I also read the downstream uses in projective-space/ProjectiveSpace/HomogeneousQuotientProj.lean and graded-rings/examples/QuotientLocalization.lean. The existing simp lemmas (gradedRingHom_apply, gradedRingHom_toRingHom, gradedDecompose_mk, coe_gradedDecomposePre) are oriented sensibly, and I saw no loop or competing-rule risk. They do not clash with Mathlib's GradedRingHom.coe_toRingHom, which has a different left-hand side. The two findings are about missing simp-interface lemmas, which I inferred from proofs that unfold definitions or destructure memberships by hand. I could not run Lean, so I do not know whether the proposed lemmas would fire exactly as intended after being added.

findings.declaration: Ideal.Quotient.gradedComponent (and its users gradedComponentGradedMonoid, gradedRingHom, gradedDecompose_rightInverse)
findings.problem: The component is an `AddSubgroup.map` of an inline structure literal. There is no membership lemma (for example `mem_gradedComponent : y ∈ gradedComponent 𝒜 I i ↔ ∃ a ∈ 𝒜 i, mk I a = y`) and no `mk_mem_gradedComponent`. Every proof therefore reaches through the definitional unfolding. Examples are `⟨_, hx, rfl⟩` in `gradedRingHom`, `rcases hx with ⟨a, ha, rfl⟩` followed by `change a ∈ 𝒜 i at ha` in `gradedComponentGradedMonoid`, and `rcases y.property with ⟨a, ha, hya⟩`. The downstream file `HomogeneousQuotientProj.lean` repeats the same `rcases hx with ⟨a, ha, rfl⟩`. `simp` has no canonical way to normalise `y ∈ gradedComponent 𝒜 I i`, and `ha` only has the right type after a `change`. This depends on the private structure literal being defeq to `𝒜 i`, so the pattern is fragile.
findings.proposed_change: Add `theorem mem_gradedComponent {i} {y : A ⧸ I} : y ∈ gradedComponent 𝒜 I i ↔ ∃ a ∈ 𝒜 i, Ideal.Quotient.mk I a = y`, tagged `@[simp]`. Its proof can be `Iff.rfl`, or `AddSubgroup.mem_map` followed by `Iff.rfl`. Add `theorem mk_mem_gradedComponent {a} (ha : a ∈ 𝒜 i) : mk I a ∈ gradedComponent 𝒜 I i`. Then rewrite the `rcases`/`change` blocks to use these lemmas.
findings.benefit: Membership in the quotient components gets a stable simp normal form (an existential over the source component). Proofs here and in the projective-space file no longer depend on defeq unfolding of the inline structure. Because `gradedComponent` is an `@[expose]` def, the interface stays usable if its body changes.

evidence.excerpt: change a ∈ 𝒜 i at ha

findings.excerpt: toFun x := ⟨Ideal.Quotient.mk I x, ⟨x, x.property, rfl⟩⟩
findings.problem: `gradedComponentMap` and `gradedDecomposePre` have no simp lemmas of their own, such as `(gradedComponentMap 𝒜 I i x : A ⧸ I) = mk I x` or the value of `gradedDecomposePre` on a homogeneous element. Later proofs instead pass the definitions to `simp` as unfolding lemmas, for example `simp [gradedDecomposePre, gradedComponentMap]` in `coe_gradedDecomposePre` and again, with `DirectSum.decompose_of_mem 𝒜 ha`, in `gradedDecompose_rightInverse`. Unfolding exposes the `DirectSum.map ∘ decomposeAddEquiv` structure and the anonymous-constructor body. `gradedDecompose_mk` rewrites to `gradedDecomposePre 𝒜 I x` and stops there, so a user of the public `gradedDecompose` has no simp path to the components of the decomposition of `mk I a` for homogeneous `a`.
findings.proposed_change: Add `@[simp] theorem coe_gradedComponentMap (x : 𝒜 i) : (gradedComponentMap 𝒜 I i x : A ⧸ I) = Ideal.Quotient.mk I x := rfl`. Add `theorem gradedDecomposePre_of_mem {i} {a} (ha : a ∈ 𝒜 i) : gradedDecomposePre 𝒜 I a = DirectSum.of _ i (gradedComponentMap 𝒜 I i ⟨a, ha⟩)`, proved from `DirectSum.decompose_of_mem`. Add a corresponding `gradedDecompose_mk_of_mem`. Then replace the `simp [gradedDecomposePre, gradedComponentMap, ...]` calls with these lemmas, so the definitions are not unfolded.
findings.benefit: The rewrite `gradedDecompose (mk I a)` to `of i (image of a)` for homogeneous `a` becomes a simp-closed chain. The internal proofs stop unfolding definitions. Users, including the projective-space development, get a canonical normal form for component images.
